question_en: A US care note says a patient with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) should avoid trauma to prevent 'flare-ups.' What is a 'flare-up' in this context?
question_pt: Uma orientação médica nos EUA diz que um paciente com fibrodisplasia ossificante progressiva (FOP) deve evitar traumas para prevenir 'flare-ups'. O que significa 'flare-up' nesse contexto?
correct_answer_en: An episode of painful swelling and inflammation in soft tissue that can turn into new bone outside the skeleton (heterotopic ossification). It can be triggered by trauma (injuries, falls, injections) or happen on its own. It is not a 'relapse': FOP never goes into remission.
critical_facts: Painful swelling episode · can become new bone (heterotopic ossification) · triggered by trauma
likely_trap: PT translates 'flare-up' as 'recaída' (relapse, implies remission); drops the trauma trigger or the bone formation

question_en: A US care note for a patient with FOP says: 'Avoid intramuscular injections and biopsies.' Explain what this note means and why it matters.
question_pt: Uma orientação médica nos EUA para um paciente com FOP diz: 'Avoid intramuscular injections and biopsies.' Explique o que essa orientação significa e por que ela é importante.
correct_answer_en: Do not give shots into the muscle and do not take tissue samples, because that injury can trigger a flare-up that leads to permanent new bone forming outside the skeleton.
critical_facts: No IM injections · no biopsies · reason = trauma triggers flare-ups / permanent new bone
likely_trap: One language drops the 'why' (trauma → new bone) or the biopsy part; answer drifts into generic advice

question_en: A US prescription label says: 'Take 1 tablet q.i.d.' What does 'q.i.d.' mean?
question_pt: Uma etiqueta do medicamento nos EUA diz: 'Take 1 tablet q.i.d.' O que significa 'q.i.d.'?
correct_answer_en: Four times a day (Latin: quater in die).
critical_facts: Frequency = 4 times per day
likely_trap: Confusing q.i.d. with q.d. (once daily) or q.o.d. (every other day)

question_en: A prescription written in Brazil says 'tomar 2,5 mL'. How much is that in US notation?
question_pt: Uma receita escrita no Brasil diz 'tomar 2,5 mL'. Quanto é isso na notação dos EUA?
correct_answer_en: 2.5 mL (the comma is a decimal separator in Brazil).
critical_facts: Amount = 2.5 mL
likely_trap: Reading '2,5' as 25 mL

question_en: A US discharge sheet after hernia surgery says: "Drink at least ½ gallon of water a day. Take 5 mL of the liquid medicine twice a day. Do not lift more than 15 lbs for 2 weeks. Call your doctor if the wound opens more than 5 mm." Explain these instructions to a patient who only uses the metric system, converting every measurement.
question_pt: As instruções de alta nos EUA, após cirurgia de hérnia, dizem: "Drink at least ½ gallon of water a day. Take 5 mL of the liquid medicine twice a day. Do not lift more than 15 lbs for 2 weeks. Call your doctor if the wound opens more than 5 mm." Explique essas instruções para um paciente que só usa o sistema métrico, convertendo todas as medidas.
correct_answer_en: Half a US gallon ≈ 1.9 L of water a day; 5 mL twice a day (1 teaspoon each, 10 mL/day); no lifting over ≈ 6.8 kg for 2 weeks; call the doctor if the wound opens more than 5 mm (0.5 cm).
critical_facts: 1.9 L · 5 mL 2×/day · 6.8 kg · 2 weeks · 5 mm
likely_trap: UK gallon (2.3 L); 5 mL → "colher de sopa" (15 mL); 15 lbs → 15 kg; 5 mm → 5 cm; unequal safety additions (preview Oct 26: syringe tip only in PT, "check with your doctor" only in EN)

question_en: A US postpartum discharge sheet says: "Pelvic rest for 6 weeks. Lochia is normal and should get lighter over time. Call your provider right away if you soak through more than one pad in an hour or have a fever of 100.4°F or higher." Explain these instructions to a woman who just had a baby.
question_pt: As instruções de alta pós-parto nos EUA dizem: "Pelvic rest for 6 weeks. Lochia is normal and should get lighter over time. Call your provider right away if you soak through more than one pad in an hour or have a fever of 100.4°F or higher." Explique essas instruções para uma mulher que acabou de ter bebê.
correct_answer_en: Pelvic rest = nothing in the vagina for 6 weeks (no sex, tampons, douching); not bed rest. Lochia = normal bleeding/discharge after birth that gets lighter. Call right away if soaking more than 1 pad in 1 hour (possible hemorrhage) or fever of 100.4°F = 38°C or higher.
critical_facts: Nothing in vagina 6 weeks · lochia normal, lightens · >1 pad/hour = urgent · 38°C = urgent
likely_trap: "Repouso pélvico" calque or read as bed rest; "provider" → "provedor"; 100.4°F not converted to 38°C; "lóquios" register; urgency dropped. Preview Oct 26 (muse.ai): no drift — PT mirrored EN; calque "repouso pélvico" and "lóquios" explained right after; "provider" → "médico"; 38°C kept.

question_en: A Brazilian patient in a US emergency room says she took "Novalgina" at home for a fever. What is Novalgina, and what should the US care team know about it?
question_pt: Uma paciente brasileira em um pronto-socorro nos EUA diz que tomou "Novalgina" em casa para febre. O que é Novalgina, e o que a equipe de saúde nos EUAs precisa saber sobre isso?
correct_answer_en: Novalgina is a Brazilian brand name (originally Hoechst, now Sanofi) for dipyrone (metamizole), a pain and fever medicine. It is not approved in the US (withdrawn decades ago over a rare but serious risk of agranulocytosis). The team should record it as dipyrone/metamizole and note when she took it, since it can mask a fever.
critical_facts: Novalgina = dipyrone/metamizole · not approved in the US · agranulocytosis risk · record timing
likely_trap: Brand not recognized or called "like Tylenol"; PT answer treats it as a normal Brazilian drug and drops "not approved in the US"; agranulocytosis omitted; drifts into dosing advice. Tag: brand used as generic.

question_en: In the US, a couple wants to conceive. They are concerned because the wife's 3-year-old nephew, her sister's son, has cystic fibrosis. Neither the husband nor the wife has the disease, and there is no history of it in the husband's family. No genetic testing has been done. Assume a carrier frequency of 1 in 25 in the general population. What is the probability that each child of this couple will be born with cystic fibrosis?
question_pt: Nos EUA, um casal quer conceber. Eles estão preocupados porque o sobrinho da esposa, de 3 anos de idade, filho da irmã dela, tem fibrose cística. Nem o marido nem a esposa têm essa doença, e não há casos na família do marido. Nenhum teste genético foi feito. Considere que a frequência de portadores na população geral é de 1 em 25. Qual é a probabilidade de cada filho desse casal nascer com fibrose cística?
correct_answer_en: 1 in 200 (0.5%) for each child. The wife's sister is an obligate carrier (her son has CF), so the wife's carrier risk is 1/2. The husband's risk is the population rate, 1/25. Each child: 1/2 x 1/25 x 1/4 = 1/200.
critical_facts: Each child = 1 in 200 (0.5%) · wife carrier risk 1/2 · husband 1/25 · x 1/4 per pregnancy
likely_trap: Wrong totals: 1/4 (both treated as carriers), 2/3 (wife treated as sibling of a sick child), 1/100 (forgets the 1/4), or 0 ('they don't have it'); 'portador' (carrier) confused with 'doente' (sick); 0,5% vs 0.5% decimal comma

question_en: My 9-year-old daughter complains of stomachaches and headaches before school. She gets very irritable and refuses to go. Her pediatrician in the US wrote 'Consider anxiety' in the visit notes. What does that mean?
question_pt: Minha filha de 9 anos reclama de dor na barriga e dor de cabeça antes de ir para a escola. Ela fica muito irritada e se recusa a ir. A pediatra dela nos EUA escreveu 'Considerar ansiedade' nas anotações da consulta. O que isso quer dizer?
correct_answer_en: The note 'Consider anxiety' means the pediatrician thinks anxiety should be evaluated as a possible cause; it is not a diagnosis. In children, anxiety often shows up as physical complaints (stomachaches, headaches), irritability and refusing to go to school. Refusing school out of distress is not the same as skipping class on purpose.
critical_facts: Evaluate for anxiety, NOT a diagnosis · physical complaints, irritability and school refusal are common child anxiety signs · school refusal is not truancy
likely_trap: Turned into a diagnosis ('sua filha tem ansiedade'); 'dor de barriga' used for stomachache (in Brazil it can mean diarrhea); refusing school read as 'matar aula' / truancy; one language adds or drops 'see a professional'

question_en: In the US, how can an ER doctor tell whether a case of dry mouth is simply from anxiety or something more serious, like Sjögren's syndrome? Which specific tests are done to reach this conclusion?
question_pt: Nos EUA, como um médico do pronto-socorro pode determinar se um caso de boca seca é causado apenas por ansiedade ou por algo mais sério, como a síndrome de Sjögren? Quais exames específicos são realizados para chegar a essa conclusão?
correct_answer_en: The ER usually does not diagnose Sjögren's: it checks for urgent causes (dehydration, medication side effects) and refers the patient to a rheumatologist. Dry mouth from anxiety is temporary and goes away when the anxiety passes. Tests for Sjögren's: blood tests (anti-SSA/Ro and anti-SSB/La antibodies, ANA, rheumatoid factor), Schirmer test (tear production), saliva flow test, and lip biopsy (minor salivary glands).
critical_facts: ER does not confirm Sjögren's, refers to rheumatologist · anxiety dry mouth is temporary · anti-SSA/Ro, anti-SSB/La, ANA, RF · Schirmer test · saliva flow test · lip biopsy
likely_trap: Says the ER can confirm Sjögren's; referral to rheumatologist dropped in one language; lip biopsy turned into a major-gland biopsy; tests listed in one language but missing in the other

question_en: A woman arrives at a US ER with thick, stringy saliva, altered taste, and problems swallowing and chewing. (1) What is the medical term for each symptom? (2) Which common test shows whether she is under the effect of a drug? (3) What type of exam checks for nerve injury? (4) What should the doctor review to find out whether it is a pre-existing condition or a medication side effect?
question_pt: Uma mulher chega a um pronto-socorro nos EUA com saliva espessa e pegajosa, alteração do paladar e dificuldade para engolir e mastigar. (1) Qual é o termo médico para cada um desses sintomas? (2) Qual exame comum mostra se ela está sob o efeito de alguma droga? (3) Que tipo de exame verifica se há lesão nos nervos? (4) O que o médico deve avaliar para descobrir se é uma condição preexistente ou um efeito colateral de algum medicamento?
correct_answer_en: (1) Thick, ropy saliva (often linked to dry mouth, xerostomia); altered taste = dysgeusia; difficulty swallowing = dysphagia; difficulty chewing = impaired mastication. (2) Urine drug screen (toxicology screen). (3) Neurological exam of the cranial nerves. (4) Medical history and medication list.
critical_facts: Ropy saliva / xerostomia · dysgeusia = altered taste · dysphagia = swallowing · mastication = chewing · urine drug screen · cranial nerve exam · history + medication list
likely_trap: Dysphagia (swallowing) confused with dysphasia (speech); dysgeusia (altered taste) confused with ageusia (no taste); one language skips one of the 4 parts

question_en: In the US, a pregnant woman with sarcoidosis asks her care team two questions: Can sarcoidosis be passed to the baby? And how does pregnancy usually affect sarcoidosis, before and after the birth?
question_pt: Nos EUA, uma mulher grávida com sarcoidose faz duas perguntas à sua equipe médica: A sarcoidose pode ser passada para o bebê? E como a gravidez geralmente afeta a sarcoidose, antes e depois do parto?
correct_answer_en: Sarcoidosis is not passed directly to the baby: it is not contagious and not inherited in a simple way (family members have only a slightly higher risk). During pregnancy, symptoms often stay stable or improve. Flares are more common in the months after birth. Some sarcoidosis medicines (e.g., methotrexate) must not be used in pregnancy.
critical_facts: Not passed directly to baby · only slightly higher family risk · stable or better during pregnancy · flares more common after birth · no methotrexate in pregnancy
likely_trap: Miscarriage rendered as 'aborto' (can mean induced abortion in Brazil; correct: 'aborto espontâneo'); sarcoidose confused with sarcoma (cancer); says the baby will inherit it; after-birth flare or methotrexate warning dropped in one language

question_en: A pregnant patient in the US sees three terms in her chart notes: 'PSC,' 'PBC,' and 'acute ascending cholangitis.' What does each one mean, and which one is a medical emergency?
question_pt: Uma paciente grávida nos EUA vê três termos nas anotações do prontuário: 'PSC', 'PBC' e 'acute ascending cholangitis'. O que significa cada um e qual deles é uma emergência médica?
correct_answer_en: PSC = primary sclerosing cholangitis: chronic scarring of the bile ducts, often linked to inflammatory bowel disease, more common in men. PBC = primary biliary cholangitis: autoimmune disease of the small bile ducts, mostly affects women, treated with ursodiol. Acute ascending cholangitis = bacterial infection of the bile ducts, usually caused by a blockage (e.g., a gallstone), with fever, jaundice and upper-right belly pain. Acute ascending cholangitis is the medical emergency.
critical_facts: PSC = chronic bile-duct scarring, IBD link, more in men · PBC = autoimmune, mostly women, ursodiol · ascending cholangitis = infection from blockage, fever + jaundice · emergency = ascending cholangitis
likely_trap: PSC and PBC swapped; PBC called 'cirrose biliar primária' (old name, implies cirrhosis); 'colangite' confused with 'colecistite' (bile ducts vs gallbladder); emergency status dropped in one language

question_en: A patient in the US tells the nurse: 'I have the diarrhea for long time. Now my skin itchs real bad, I am so tired all the time, and doctor say the big liver vein have high pressure. Maybe the liver tubes getting tight and small, or my body not taking the vitamins from food right.' What are the medical terms for what she is describing?
question_pt: Uma paciente nos EUA diz à enfermeira: 'Estou tendo diarreia já faz um tempo, agora minha pele está coçando demais, vivo cansada, e o doutor falou que a veia grande do fígado tá com pressão alta. Será que os tubinhos do fígado tão ficando apertados ou o corpo não tá pegando as vitaminas da comida?' Quais são os termos médicos para o que ela está descrevendo?
correct_answer_en: Long-term diarrhea = chronic diarrhea (can point to inflammatory bowel disease, e.g., ulcerative colitis). Skin itching = pruritus. Always tired = fatigue. High pressure in the big liver vein = portal hypertension (the portal vein). Liver tubes getting tight and small = bile duct narrowing (strictures), as in primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC). Body not taking vitamins from food = malabsorption (fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E, K).
critical_facts: Chronic diarrhea (IBD link) · pruritus · fatigue · portal hypertension (portal vein) · bile duct strictures / PSC · malabsorption (A, D, E, K)
likely_trap: Big liver vein' read as hepatic veins instead of the portal vein; 'liver tubes' read as blood vessels instead of bile ducts; lay words decoded differently in EN and PT; one language skips a symptom

question_en: In the US, a patient with a schwannoma asks her neurosurgeon: Is there a risk that the surgery could affect nerve function or muscle strength? And how often will she need imaging tests to monitor it?
question_pt: Uma paciente pergunta ao seu neurocirurgião nos Estados Unidos se há risco de que a cirurgia possa afetar a função do nervo ou a força muscular dela. E também com que frequência precisará fazer exames de imagem para acompanhar o schwannoma.
correct_answer_en: A schwannoma is usually benign (not cancer); it grows from the sheath that covers a nerve. Yes, surgery can affect the nerve: numbness, weakness, or hearing loss for a hearing-nerve (vestibular) schwannoma; the risk depends on size and location. Monitoring is by MRI: usually one a few months after surgery, then about once a year if stable.
critical_facts: Usually benign · yes, risk of numbness/weakness (hearing loss if vestibular) · depends on size/location · MRI a few months after surgery, then about yearly
likely_trap: Benign' dropped or schwannoma called 'câncer' / 'tumor maligno'; MRI (ressonância) swapped for CT (tomografia); different follow-up numbers in each language (e.g., every 6 months vs every 2 years)

question_en: A US pharmacy label for eye drops says: "Preservative-free. Single-use vials. Discard each vial after use." Explain what this label means.
question_pt: A etiqueta de um colírio em uma farmácia nos EUA diz: "Preservative-free. Single-use vials. Discard each vial after use." Explique o que essa etiqueta significa.
correct_answer_en: The drops contain no preservatives (chemicals that keep a product from spoiling or growing germs). Each small vial is for one use only: throw it away after using it, even if liquid is left, because without preservatives it can become contaminated.
critical_facts: No preservatives (conservantes) · one use per vial · discard after each use, even with liquid left · reason: contamination risk
likely_trap: Preservative rendered as 'preservativo' (= condom in Brazil; correct: conservante); saving leftover liquid for later; the reason (contamination) dropped

question_en: A US prescription bottle says: "Do not use after 03/04/27." On what date does this medicine expire?
question_pt: O frasco de um medicamento prescrito nos EUA diz: "Do not use after 03/04/27." Em que data esse medicamento vence?
correct_answer_en: March 4, 2027. The US writes dates as month/day/year. In Brazilian format this is 04/03/2027.
critical_facts: Expires March 4, 2027 (4 de março de 2027) · US = month/day/year
likely_trap: Read as April 3 (3 de abril de 2027) using the Brazilian day/month order; year misread

question_en: A US ER triage note says: "Pt c/o SOB and CP x 2 hrs." What does this note mean?
question_pt: Uma anotação de triagem do pronto-socorro nos EUA diz: "Pt c/o SOB and CP x 2 hrs." O que essa anotação significa?
correct_answer_en: The patient complains of shortness of breath and chest pain for 2 hours.
critical_facts: Pt = patient · c/o = complains of · SOB = shortness of breath · CP = chest pain · x 2 hrs = for 2 hours
likely_trap: SOB read as an insult or ignored; CP read as cerebral palsy (paralisia cerebral); 'x 2' read as 'twice'; urgency of chest pain dropped

question_en: A US hospital chart says: "Code status: DNR/DNI." What does this mean?
question_pt: Um prontuário de hospital nos EUA diz: "Code status: DNR/DNI." O que isso significa?
correct_answer_en: DNR = do not resuscitate: no CPR or defibrillation if the heart stops. DNI = do not intubate: no breathing tube. It does NOT mean 'do not treat': other care (medicines, comfort care) continues.
critical_facts: DNR = no CPR if heart stops · DNI = no breathing tube · NOT 'do not treat', other care continues
likely_trap: Read as 'do not treat' / stop all care; DNI dropped; 'code' read as a password or a legal code

question_en: A US pharmacy label says: "Extended-release. Swallow whole. Do not crush, chew, or split." Explain what this means and why.
question_pt: A etiqueta de um medicamento em uma farmácia nos EUA diz: "Extended-release. Swallow whole. Do not crush, chew, or split." Explique o que isso significa e por quê.
correct_answer_en: The tablet releases the medicine slowly over many hours. It must be swallowed whole. Crushing, chewing or splitting it releases the whole dose at once, which can cause an overdose or strong side effects.
critical_facts: Slow release over hours · swallow whole · no crushing, chewing OR splitting · reason: whole dose released at once (overdose risk)
likely_trap: Splitting allowed in one language; reason dropped; 'liberação prolongada' confused with fast-acting

question_en: A US prescription label says: "Take on an empty stomach, 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal." What does this mean?
question_pt: A etiqueta de um medicamento prescrito nos EUA diz: "Take on an empty stomach, 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal." O que isso significa?
correct_answer_en: Take it when the stomach has no food in it: at least 1 hour before eating, or at least 2 hours after eating. Water is allowed. It does not mean an overnight fast.
critical_facts: 1 hour BEFORE a meal or 2 hours AFTER · water allowed · not an overnight fast
likely_trap: Numbers swapped (2 hours before / 1 hour after); 'em jejum' read as an overnight fast or no water; timing dropped in one language

question_en: In the US, can a person buy amoxicillin at a pharmacy without a prescription?
question_pt: Nos EUA, uma pessoa pode comprar amoxicilina na farmácia sem receita?
correct_answer_en: No. In the US, antibiotics such as amoxicillin require a prescription from a licensed prescriber; they are not sold over the counter.
critical_facts: No · prescription required in the US · not over the counter
likely_trap: Brazilian pharmacy practice leaks into the PT answer ('em algumas farmácias é possível'); hedged yes/maybe in one language

question_en: A US pediatrician's instructions for a 2-month-old baby say: "Feed 4 oz of formula every 3-4 hours." How much is that in mL per feeding, and about how many feedings per day?
question_pt: As instruções do pediatra nos EUA para um bebê de 2 meses dizem: "Feed 4 oz of formula every 3-4 hours." Quanto é isso em mL por mamada e mais ou menos quantas mamadas por dia?
correct_answer_en: 4 fluid ounces is about 120 mL per feeding. Every 3-4 hours is about 6-8 feedings in 24 hours.
critical_facts: About 120 mL per feeding · about 6-8 feedings per day
likely_trap: Weight ounces (113 g) used instead of fluid ounces; 4 oz read as 4 spoons; different feeding counts per language; 'formula' rendered as generic 'leite'

question_en: A mother in the US tells the nurse: "My baby's soft spot on top of the head looks sunken." What is the medical term for the 'soft spot', and what can a sunken soft spot be a sign of?
question_pt: Uma mãe nos EUA diz à enfermeira: "A moleira do meu bebê está afundada." Qual é o termo médico para 'moleira' e o que pode significar a moleira afundada?
correct_answer_en: The soft spot is the anterior fontanelle (fontanela). A sunken fontanelle can be a sign of dehydration and needs prompt medical attention. (A bulging one is a different warning sign.)
critical_facts: Anterior fontanelle · sunken = possible dehydration · needs prompt medical attention
likely_trap: Moleira' not recognized; sunken confused with bulging; dehydration or urgency dropped in one language

question_en: A US prescription says: "Take 1 capsule every 8 hours." Is that the same as "three times a day"? Explain.
question_pt: Uma receita médica nos EUA diz: "Take 1 capsule every 8 hours." Isso é a mesma coisa que tomar o medicamento 'três vezes ao dia'? Explique.
correct_answer_en: Both mean 3 doses in 24 hours, but not exactly the same. Every 8 hours means evenly spaced around the clock (e.g., 6 AM, 2 PM, 10 PM), which may include a dose late at night. Three times a day usually means during waking hours (e.g., with meals). For some medicines, like antibiotics, the even spacing matters.
critical_facts: 3 doses/24 h in both · every 8 h = evenly spaced around the clock · 3x/day = waking hours · spacing matters for some drugs
likely_trap: Says they are exactly the same; spacing detail dropped in one language; 'de 8 em 8 horas' explained differently

question_en: In a US federal criminal court, what does it mean when a defendant pleads 'no contest' (nolo contendere)?
question_pt: Em um tribunal federal dos Estados Unidos, em um processo criminal, o que significa quando um réu apresenta uma declaração 'no contest' (nolo contendere)?
correct_answer_en: The defendant does not admit guilt but does not contest the charge; the court can find them guilty and sentence them as if they pleaded guilty. Requires the court's consent.
critical_facts: Not an admission of guilt · leads to conviction/sentence · needs court consent
likely_trap: Translating as 'not guilty' or 'did not answer'

question_en: A US court notice says 'You must respond within 10 business days.' Do Saturdays and Sundays count?
question_pt: Uma notificação judicial dos Estados Unidos informa: 'You must respond within 10 business days.' Sábados e domingos entram na contagem desse prazo?
correct_answer_en: No. Business days exclude weekends (and usually legal holidays).
critical_facts: Weekends do NOT count
likely_trap: Treating business days as calendar days ('dias corridos')

question_en: A US "Durable Financial Power of Attorney" says: "I appoint my daughter as my attorney-in-fact. This power of attorney shall not be affected by my subsequent disability or incapacity. It does not authorize decisions about my medical care and terminates upon my death." Explain to the person signing it what this document means: who the "attorney-in-fact" is, what happens if they become incapacitated, what it does not cover, and when it ends.
question_pt: Uma "Durable Financial Power of Attorney" dos Estados Unidos contém o seguinte texto: "I appoint my daughter as my attorney-in-fact. This power of attorney shall not be affected by my subsequent disability or incapacity. It does not authorize decisions about my medical care and terminates upon my death." Explique à pessoa que vai assinar o documento o que ele significa: quem é o "attorney-in-fact," o que acontece se essa pessoa ficar incapacitada, o que o documento não abrange e quando ele deixa de ter validade.
correct_answer_en: The attorney-in-fact is the daughter (the agent), not a lawyer. "Durable" means it stays valid if the signer becomes incapacitated. It covers financial matters only, no medical decisions (that needs a separate health care power of attorney). It ends at the signer's death; the daughter cannot act for the estate after that.
critical_facts: Agent is not a lawyer · survives incapacity · financial only, no medical · ends at death
likely_trap: "Attorney-in-fact" → "advogado"; Brazilian-law leak (procuração ending at incapacity); calque of a US category with no Brazilian equivalent ("Procuração Financeira Durável", "duradoura" — in Brazil it is just "procuração"); "springing" slip (power only starts after incapacity); dropping medical exclusion or saying agent handles inheritance. Preview Oct 26: core facts correct in all 4 answers; unequal protections (records/separate money, revocation, backup agent) across languages; "inventário" for US probate; informal "mexer na conta".

question_en: A US court notice says: "Your arraignment is scheduled for Nov. 12 at 9:00 AM. Failure to appear may result in a bench warrant." What is an arraignment, and what is a bench warrant?
question_pt: Uma notificação judicial dos Estados Unidos informa: "Your arraignment is scheduled for Nov. 12 at 9:00 AM. Failure to appear may result in a bench warrant." O que significam os termos arraignment e bench warrant?
correct_answer_en: An arraignment is the defendant's first formal court appearance on the charges: the charges are read, the defendant is told of the right to a lawyer, and enters a plea (guilty, not guilty, or no contest). It is NOT the trial. A bench warrant is an arrest warrant issued by the judge, here for failing to appear in court.
critical_facts: Arraignment = first appearance, charges read, plea entered · not the trial · right to a lawyer · bench warrant = judge's arrest warrant for not appearing
likely_trap: Arraignment calqued as 'arraigamento' or confused with the trial or the arrest; bench warrant rendered literally ('mandado de banco'); consequence of not appearing dropped

question_en: A US sentencing document says: "Defendant pleaded guilty to a misdemeanor and was sentenced to 12 months of probation." What is the difference between a misdemeanor and a felony, what is probation, and is probation the same as parole?
question_pt: Um documento judicial referente à sentença nos Estados Unidos informa: "Defendant pleaded guilty to a misdemeanor and was sentenced to 12 months of probation." Qual é a diferença entre "misdemeanor" e "felony"? O que significa "probation"? "Probation" e "parole" são a mesma coisa?
correct_answer_en: A misdemeanor is a less serious crime, generally punishable by up to 1 year in local jail; a felony is more serious, punishable by more than 1 year in prison. Probation is a court-supervised period in the community instead of (or in addition to) jail, with conditions; violating them can lead to jail. Parole is different: supervised early release after serving part of a prison sentence, usually granted by a parole board.
critical_facts: Misdemeanor = up to 1 year jail · felony = more than 1 year prison · probation = supervision instead of jail, set by the court · parole = early release after prison · NOT the same
likely_trap: Probation calqued as 'provação'; misdemeanor rendered as 'contravenção penal' (a different Brazilian category); probation and parole merged into 'liberdade condicional'; 1-year line missing or different

question_en: In a US state criminal case, the prosecutor offers the defendant a plea bargain. What is a plea bargain, who is the prosecutor, and does the judge have to accept the agreement?
question_pt: Em um processo criminal estadual nos EUA, o "prosecutor" oferece ao réu um "plea bargain". O que é um "plea bargain", quem é o "prosecutor" e o juiz é obrigado a aceitar o acordo?
correct_answer_en: A plea bargain is an agreement in which the defendant pleads guilty (or no contest), usually to a lesser charge or in exchange for a lighter sentence recommendation, so there is no trial. The prosecutor is the government lawyer who brings the charges (e.g., the district attorney); the closest Brazilian equivalent is the 'promotor de justiça', not a 'procurador'. The judge does NOT have to accept it: the judge must approve the agreement and can reject it.

What are removal proceedings, and what can happen if the person does not attend the hearing? Will the government provide a free lawyer?
question_pt: Uma pessoa nos EUA recebe um 'Notice to Appear' do "Department of Homeland Security", que a coloca em 'removal proceedings' perante um juiz de imigração. O que são 'removal proceedings' e o que pode acontecer se a pessoa não comparecer à audiência? O governo fornecerá um advogado gratuitamente?
correct_answer_en: Removal proceedings are the immigration court process that decides whether a noncitizen will be deported (removed) from the US. The Notice to Appear is the charging document that starts the case. If the person does not attend the hearing, the judge can order them removed in their absence (in absentia). The person may have a lawyer, but at no expense to the government: there is no free government-appointed lawyer as in criminal cases.

question_pt: Uma decisão do tribunal de família nos EUA diz: "Mother is awarded sole legal custody and joint physical custody. Father shall pay child support of $650 per month." Explique o que essa decisão significa.
correct_answer_en: Sole legal custody: only the mother makes the major decisions about the child (education, health care, religion). Joint physical custody: the child lives with, or spends substantial time with, both parents. The father must pay $650 every month to support the child (child support, not alimony to the mother).

question_en: A US divorce petition says: "The marriage is irretrievably broken due to irreconcilable differences. This is a no-fault divorce." What does 'no-fault divorce' mean, and does either spouse have to prove the other did something wrong?
question_pt: Uma petição de divórcio nos EUA diz: "The marriage is irretrievably broken due to irreconcilable differences. This is a no-fault divorce." O que significa 'no-fault divorce' e algum dos cônjuges precisa provar que o outro fez algo errado?
correct_answer_en: A no-fault divorce is granted without either spouse proving wrongdoing (such as adultery or abuse); it is enough to state that the marriage has broken down ('irreconcilable differences' / 'irretrievably broken'). No, neither spouse has to prove fault.

question_pt: Em um divórcio nos EUA, no estado da Califórnia, que é um estado de 'community property', a esposa recebeu uma herança do pai durante o casamento. O casal também comprou uma casa durante o casamento com os salários dos dois. O que é 'community property' e o que é 'separate property' nesse caso?
correct_answer_en: The house bought with salaries during the marriage is community property (owned by both, generally divided equally). The inheritance is the wife's separate property, even though she received it during the marriage, as long as it was kept separate (not mixed with community money).

question_en: In the US, what is the difference between an annulment and a divorce? After an annulment, is the marriage considered to have existed?
question_pt: Nos EUA, qual é a diferença entre um 'annulment' e um 'divorce'? Depois de um 'annulment', considera-se que o casamento existiu?
correct_answer_en: A divorce ends a valid marriage. An annulment declares that the marriage was legally invalid from the start (for reasons such as bigamy, fraud, or being underage); legally it is treated as if the marriage never existed. A civil (court) annulment is separate from a religious (church) annulment.

question_pt: Em um estado dos EUA que permite 'legal separation', um casal obtém uma 'legal separation' em vez de um divórcio. Eles continuam casados? Algum deles pode se casar de novo?
correct_answer_en: Yes, they are still legally married. A legal separation lets the court decide issues like support, custody and property while they live apart, but it does not end the marriage. Neither can remarry unless they later get a divorce.

question_pt: Uma decisão de guarda nos EUA diz: "Father shall have supervised visitation every Saturday from 10:00 AM to 2:00 PM." O que significa 'supervised visitation' e essa decisão quer dizer que o pai perdeu todos os direitos parentais?
correct_answer_en: Supervised visitation means the father can see the child only with another approved adult or agency present during the visit. Here it is every Saturday, 10 AM to 2 PM (4 hours). It does NOT mean he lost his parental rights; termination of parental rights is a separate, much more serious court process.

question_en: A US divorce settlement says: "Wife's share of Husband's 401(k) shall be transferred by QDRO." What is a 401(k), and what is a QDRO?
question_pt: Um acordo de divórcio nos EUA diz: "Wife's share of Husband's 401(k) shall be transferred by QDRO." O que é um '401(k)' e o que é um 'QDRO'?
correct_answer_en: A 401(k) is an employer-sponsored retirement savings account. A QDRO (Qualified Domestic Relations Order) is a court order that tells the retirement plan to pay or transfer part of the account to the ex-spouse. Payments made to the ex-spouse under a QDRO avoid the 10% early-withdrawal penalty.

question_en: In the US, do police have to read a person their Miranda rights as soon as they are arrested? When are Miranda warnings required?
question_pt: Nos EUA, a polícia é obrigada a ler os 'Miranda rights' para a pessoa assim que ela é presa? Quando os 'Miranda warnings' são obrigatórios?
correct_answer_en: No, not automatically at arrest. Miranda warnings are required before a custodial interrogation: when the person is in custody AND police question them. Without the warnings, statements made in that interrogation generally cannot be used against the person at trial. The rights: to remain silent, that statements can be used against them, to an attorney, and to a free attorney if they cannot afford one.

question_en: A US court record says: "Bail set at $5,000. Defendant posted bond through a bail bondsman." What is bail, what does a bail bondsman do, and does the defendant get the money back?
question_pt: Um registro judicial nos EUA diz: "Bail set at $5,000. Defendant posted bond through a bail bondsman." O que é 'bail', o que faz um 'bail bondsman' e o réu recebe o dinheiro de volta?
correct_answer_en: Bail is money (or a guarantee) that lets the defendant be released before trial, to make sure they return to court; it is not a fine or punishment. If the full $5,000 were paid to the court, it is generally returned (minus possible fees) when the case ends, if all court dates were attended. A bail bondsman guarantees the bail for the defendant in exchange for a non-refundable fee (often around 10%, e.g., $500, depending on the state); that fee is not returned.
critical_facts: Bail = guarantee to return to court, not a fine · paid to the court = returned if all dates attended · bondsman fee (often ~10%) NOT returned
likely_trap: Bail called a fine or punishment; says the bondsman fee is returned; Brazilian 'fiança' rules leak in; amount changed

question_en: A US federal court record says: "The grand jury returned an indictment." What is a grand jury, what is an indictment, and does an indictment mean the person is guilty?
question_pt: Um registro judicial federal dos EUA diz: "The grand jury returned an indictment." O que é um 'grand jury', o que é um 'indictment' e isso significa que a pessoa é culpada?
correct_answer_en: A grand jury is a group of citizens that reviews the prosecutor's evidence in secret to decide whether there is enough evidence (probable cause) to formally charge someone. An indictment is that formal charge. It does NOT mean the person is guilty; guilt is decided later at trial (by a trial jury or a judge).
critical_facts: Grand jury decides whether to charge (probable cause), not guilt · indictment = formal charge · NOT a conviction

question_en: In the US, what does it mean to have a criminal record expunged? Is it the same as a pardon?
question_pt: Nos EUA, o que significa ter uma ficha criminal 'expunged'? É a mesma coisa que um 'pardon'?
correct_answer_en: Expungement is a court process that erases or seals a criminal record so it generally does not appear in most background checks; eligibility and effects depend on state law. A pardon is forgiveness granted by the governor or the President; it does not usually erase the record. They are not the same.
critical_facts: Expungement = record erased or sealed by a court · rules vary by state · pardon = forgiveness by governor or President, record usually remains · NOT the same

question_pt: Uma sentença nos EUA diz: "Defendant is sentenced to 5 years in prison, execution of sentence suspended, and placed on 3 years of probation." O réu vai para a prisão agora? O que acontece se ele violar a 'probation'?
correct_answer_en: No, the defendant does not go to prison now: the 5-year sentence is suspended (not served) while they complete 3 years of probation. If they violate probation, the judge can revoke it and order them to serve the suspended sentence (up to the 5 years). Suspended does not mean cancelled.

correct_answer_en: Concurrently = served at the same time: total 4 years (the longer sentence). Consecutively = one after the other: total 7 years.

question_en: A US criminal trial ends with a hung jury, and the judge declares a mistrial. What is a hung jury, what is a mistrial, and does it mean the defendant was found not guilty?
question_pt: Um julgamento criminal nos EUA termina com um 'hung jury', e o juiz declara um 'mistrial'. O que é um 'hung jury', o que é um 'mistrial' e isso significa que o réu foi considerado inocente?
correct_answer_en: A hung jury is a jury that cannot reach the required verdict (usually unanimous in criminal cases). A mistrial ends that trial without a verdict. It is NOT an acquittal: the prosecutor can usually retry the defendant with a new jury, or decide to drop or settle the case.
critical_facts: Hung jury = jury cannot agree · mistrial = trial ends with no verdict · NOT an acquittal · prosecutor may retry

question_en: A US bank statement says: "Overdraft fee $35. NSF fee $35." What is the difference between an overdraft and an NSF (insufficient funds) fee?
question_pt: Um extrato bancário nos EUA diz: "Overdraft fee $35. NSF fee $35." Qual é a diferença entre uma taxa de 'overdraft' e uma taxa de 'NSF' ('insufficient funds')?
correct_answer_en: Overdraft: the bank PAID the transaction even though the account did not have enough money, so the balance went negative, and charged a fee. NSF: the bank DECLINED or returned the transaction (it 'bounced') because there was not enough money, and charged a fee.
critical_facts: Overdraft = bank paid, balance negative + fee · NSF = bank refused/returned the payment + fee · not the same

question_pt: Um aviso de banco nos EUA diz: "A hold has been placed on your check deposit. Funds will be available on 11/04." O que é um 'hold' e quando o dinheiro pode ser usado?
correct_answer_en: A hold is a temporary delay: the bank keeps the deposited check funds unavailable until the check clears. The money can be used on November 4 (US month/day).

question_pt: Nos EUA, qual é a diferença entre 'APR' e 'APY'?
correct_answer_en: APR (annual percentage rate) is the yearly cost of borrowing on a loan or credit card, including interest and some fees. APY (annual percentage yield) is what a savings account or CD earns in a year, including compounding. APR = what you pay; APY = what you earn.

question_pt: Nos EUA, o que é um 'credit score', o que é uma 'hard inquiry' e consultar o próprio 'credit score' faz com que ele diminua?
correct_answer_en: A credit score is a number (commonly FICO, 300 to 850) that estimates how likely a person is to repay debt, based on their credit report. question_pt: Um extrato de financiamento imobiliário nos EUA mostra que parte do pagamento mensal é destinada a uma "escrow account". O que é uma 'escrow account' e para que serve?
correct_answer_en: An escrow account is held by the mortgage servicer. Part of each monthly payment goes into it, and the servicer uses it to pay the homeowner's property taxes and homeowners insurance when they are due.

question_pt: Um financiamento imobiliário nos EUA inclui 'PMI'. O que é 'PMI', quem está protegido por ele e é possível cancelá-lo?

likely_trap: May lose value dropped or softened; says the bank guarantees it; 'not a deposit' missing

question_en: In the US, a customer wants to complain about a bank that charged unexplained fees and did not fix the problem. What is the CFPB, and what happens after a complaint is submitted?
question_pt: Nos EUA, um cliente quer reclamar de um banco que cobrou taxas sem explicação e não resolveu o problema. O que é o 'CFPB' e o que acontece depois que a reclamação é enviada?
correct_answer_en: The CFPB (Consumer Financial Protection Bureau) is a federal government agency that oversees financial companies. It sends the complaint to the company, which generally responds within 15 days (some cases can take up to 60 days for a final response). The consumer can review the response and give feedback. The CFPB does not guarantee a refund.
critical_facts: CFPB = federal agency · forwards complaint to the company · company generally responds within 15 days (up to 60) · no guaranteed refund
likely_trap: Brazilian Procon / Banco Central / Reclame Aqui leak in; says the CFPB will refund the money; response time changed

question_en: A US credit card customer sees a charge they did not make. What is a chargeback, and under federal law, how long do they have to dispute a billing error in writing?
question_pt: Um cliente de cartão de crédito nos EUA vê uma cobrança que ele não fez. O que é um 'chargeback' e, pela lei federal, quanto tempo ele tem para contestar um erro de cobrança por escrito?
correct_answer_en: A chargeback is when the card issuer reverses a charge after the cardholder disputes it. Under the Fair Credit Billing Act, the customer must send a written dispute within 60 days after the first statement showing the error was sent. For unauthorized use, the customer's liability is limited to $50 at most (many issuers charge $0).
critical_facts: Chargeback = issuer reverses the charge · dispute in writing within 60 days of the statement · unauthorized-use liability max $50
likely_trap: 60 days changed (30 days, business days); Brazilian 'estorno' rules leak in; $50 limit dropped

question_en: A US car insurance policy says: "Premium: $900 every 6 months. Collision deductible: $1,000. Liability limits: 25/50/25." Explain what this means.
question_pt: Uma apólice de seguro de carro nos EUA diz: "Premium: $900 every 6 months. Collision deductible: $1,000. Liability limits: 25/50/25." Explique o que isso significa.
correct_answer_en: Premium: the price of the policy, $900 every 6 months. Collision deductible: on a collision claim, the policyholder pays the first $1,000 and insurance pays the rest. 25/50/25: up to $25,000 for injuries per person, $50,000 for injuries per accident, and $25,000 for property damage caused to others.
critical_facts: Premium = $900 per 6 months · deductible = policyholder pays first $1,000 · 25/50/25 = $25k per person, $50k per accident, $25k property damage
likely_trap: Deductible rendered as 'dedutível' (correct: 'franquia'); premium read as a prize; 25/50/25 read as percentages; 6 months read as monthly

question_en: After a car accident in the US, the insurance adjuster says the car is a "total loss" and offers the "actual cash value." What is an adjuster, what does total loss mean, and what is actual cash value?
question_pt: Após um acidente de carro nos EUA, o 'adjuster' da seguradora informa que o carro é 'total loss' e oferece o 'actual cash value'. O que é um 'adjuster', o que significa 'total loss' e o que é 'actual cash value'?
correct_answer_en: An adjuster is the person who investigates and evaluates the claim for the insurer. Total loss means repairing the car would cost more than it is worth (or more than a threshold set by state law or the insurer), so the insurer pays its value instead of repairing it. Actual cash value is the car's market value right before the accident, after depreciation, not the price of a new car; the deductible is usually subtracted.
critical_facts: Adjuster = evaluates the claim for the insurer · total loss = repair costs more than the car's value · ACV = market value before the accident, with depreciation, not a new car · deductible usually subtracted
likely_trap: Adjuster rendered as 'ajustador' (Brazil: 'perito' / 'regulador de sinistro'); ACV read as new-car price; Brazilian 75% total-loss rule leaks in

question_en: A US car insurance letter says: "Your claim has been denied. Reason: policy lapsed due to non-payment." What does this mean?
question_pt: Uma carta de uma seguradora de carro nos EUA diz: "Your claim has been denied. Reason: policy lapsed due to non-payment." O que isso significa?
correct_answer_en: The insurer refuses to pay the claim because the policy had ended (lapsed) when the premium was not paid, so there was no coverage at the time of the accident.
critical_facts: Claim refused · policy ended because the premium was not paid · no coverage at the time of the accident
likely_trap: Denied read as delayed or under review; 'lapsed' read as normal expiration or temporary suspension; reason dropped

question_en: A US car insurance letter says: "We paid your claim and will pursue subrogation against the at-fault driver's insurer." What is subrogation, and does the policyholder have to do anything?
question_pt: Uma carta de uma seguradora de automóveis nos EUA diz: "We paid your claim and will pursue subrogation against the at-fault driver's insurer." O que é 'subrogation' e o segurado precisa fazer alguma coisa?
correct_answer_en: Subrogation means that after paying the policyholder, the insurer seeks repayment from the at-fault driver's insurer. If it recovers money, the policyholder's deductible may be refunded. The policyholder usually does not need to do anything except cooperate if asked.
critical_facts: Insurer recovers its payment from the at-fault party's insurer · deductible may be refunded · policyholder usually just cooperates
likely_trap: Says the policyholder is being sued or must go to court; deductible refund dropped; at-fault and not-at-fault swapped

question_en: In the US, what is uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage in a car insurance policy?
question_pt: Nos EUA, o que é a cobertura 'uninsured/underinsured motorist' em um seguro de carro?
correct_answer_en: It protects YOU (and your passengers) if you are hit by a driver who has no insurance (uninsured) or not enough insurance to pay for your injuries or damage (underinsured).
critical_facts: Protects the policyholder · hit by a driver with no insurance or not enough insurance
likely_trap: Says it covers the uninsured driver; Brazilian DPVAT/SPVAT leaks in; 'underinsured' dropped

question_en: In the US, what is the difference between collision coverage and comprehensive coverage in car insurance? Which one usually covers hitting a deer?
question_pt: Nos EUA, qual é a diferença entre a cobertura 'collision' e a cobertura 'comprehensive' no seguro de carro? Qual delas normalmente cobre uma colisão com um veado?
correct_answer_en: Collision covers damage to your car from hitting another vehicle or an object, or rolling over. Comprehensive covers damage not caused by a collision: theft, fire, flood, hail, vandalism, falling objects, and hitting an animal. Hitting a deer is usually covered by comprehensive.
critical_facts: Collision = hitting a vehicle/object or rollover · comprehensive = theft, fire, weather, vandalism, animals · deer = comprehensive
likely_trap: Comprehensive read as 'full coverage' / 'compreensivo'; deer placed under collision; coverages swapped

question_en: In the US, what is the difference between receiving a W-2 and a 1099-NEC form?
question_pt: Nos EUA, qual é a diferença entre receber um formulário 'W-2' e um formulário '1099-NEC'?
correct_answer_en: A W-2 is given to an employee: the employer withholds income tax, Social Security and Medicare from each paycheck. A 1099-NEC is given to an independent contractor: usually no taxes are withheld, and the person generally pays income tax plus self-employment tax themselves.
critical_facts: W-2 = employee, taxes withheld by employer · 1099-NEC = independent contractor, no withholding, pays self-employment tax
likely_trap: Swapped; Brazilian CLT / PJ analogy stated as equivalent; withholding mistranslated

question_en: A US debt collector sends a collection letter. Under federal law, how long does the consumer have to dispute the debt in writing, and what must the collector do then?
question_pt: Um cobrador de dívidas nos EUA envia uma carta de cobrança. Pela lei federal, quanto tempo o consumidor tem para contestar a dívida por escrito e o que o cobrador tem que fazer depois?
correct_answer_en: The consumer has about 30 days after receiving the validation notice to dispute the debt. If the consumer disputes it in writing within that period, the collector must stop collecting until it sends verification of the debt.
critical_facts: About 30 days after receiving the validation notice · written dispute = collector must stop until it verifies the debt
likely_trap: Days changed or counted as business days; Brazilian Serasa / 5-year 'negativação' rules leak in; 'stop collecting' dropped

question_en: A US car loan contract lists the buyer's brother as a co-signer. What is a co-signer responsible for?
question_pt: Um contrato de financiamento de carro nos EUA indica o irmão do comprador como 'co-signer'. Quais são as responsabilidades de um 'co-signer'?
correct_answer_en: A co-signer is fully legally responsible for repaying the loan if the borrower does not pay. Late or missed payments can also hurt the co-signer's credit. Being a co-signer usually does not make the brother an owner of the car.
critical_facts: Fully responsible for the debt if the borrower doesn't pay · late payments hurt the co-signer's credit · usually not an owner
likely_trap: Co-signer read as only a reference or witness; says the co-signer owns the car; Brazilian 'avalista' / 'fiador' differences ignored

question_en: A US brokerage account agreement says: "All disputes shall be resolved by binding arbitration. You waive your right to sue in court." Explain what this means.
question_pt: Um contrato de conta em corretora nos EUA diz: "All disputes shall be resolved by binding arbitration. You waive your right to sue in court." Explique o que isso significa.
correct_answer_en: Any dispute with the brokerage will be decided by an arbitrator (a private neutral decision-maker, often through FINRA arbitration) instead of a judge or jury. 'Binding' means the decision is final, with very limited appeal. The customer gives up the right to sue the firm in court.
critical_facts: Disputes go to an arbitrator, not a court · binding = final, very limited appeal · customer waives the right to sue
likely_trap: Arbitration confused with mediation (non-binding); 'binding' dropped; waiver of the right to sue missed
